one_sentence_failure_summary: YouTube's sign-in/bot-detection requirement permanently blocked video download, and the agent's only recovery was a 130-step retry loop of increasingly malformed yt-dlp commands (boolean flags passed as positional args, contradictory flags, forced generic extractor) that never resolved authentication and never produced solution.txt.
t_err_evidence: ERROR: [youtube] ZCbvyPbhRfA: Sign in to confirm you're not a bot. Use --cookies-from-browser or --cookies
t_commit_evidence: Once the YouTube auth block manifests at step 15, the outcome is locked in: the environment has no browser cookies to provide, no JS runtime is available, and no alternative download strategy (Invidious, direct API, manual transcript) is ever attempted. From step 15 onward the agent loops exclusively on yt-dlp variations that all hit the same fundamental barrier.
t_surface_evidence: ERROR: [youtube] Sign in to confirm you're not a bot ... [The command completed with exit code 1.]
trigger_explanation: The YouTube authentication requirement is a genuine environment constraint (no browser cookies available in a headless Docker container, no JS runtime). The agent recognizes the error but handles it wrongly: it tries non-existent browsers (Firefox, Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, Edge, Safari) for cookie extraction, then pivots to accumulating dozens of irrelevant flags (boolean flag values passed as positional args, contradictory mode flags, forced generic extractor) rather than seeking an alternative video source or transcript API. The core blocker is never resolved.
